verdict.reasoning: Both check sample power, threshold structure, name the underpowered-plus-favorable-threshold failure mode, and give concrete fixes, but Document 2 more explicitly names the asymmetric operationalization (only 'stop' has a crisp statistic while 'proceed/inconclusive' does not) as the core mechanism producing a de facto proceed default, and adds a distinct framing-mismatch check distinguishing the actual forced-choice instrument from the predicted-score-vs-actual description in the task, directly hitting the rubric's 'adjacent things it might measure instead' criterion. Document 1's new findings (cold-guess CI, non-binding n=36 trigger) are solid but slightly less central to the core stop-vs-proceed structural question than Document 2's three-mechanism synthesis.

Both independently recompute power at n=18 and n=36 (matching figures), correctly find the stop branch is real but only ~26-42% powered so 'proceed' is the structural default, and both flag the framing mismatch between the task's stated instrument and the one-pager's actual forced-choice hit-rate test plus concrete fixes (binding trigger, cutoff, propagation). Document 2 adds a sharper new quantification (Clopper-Pearson CI on the n=10 calibration group showing its noise can shift the primary threshold), giving it slightly more novel rigor, but Document 1's three-mechanism synthesis (power/asymmetric operationalization/ungated prose) is equally complete and well-argued, so the two are effectively tied in rubric coverage.
